claims.text: ICD 906 D.9 names 'The Director of the ODNI Controlled Access Program Central Office (CAPCO)' as 'the accountable official responsible for the implementation of this policy and for issuing IC Standards (ICS), consistent with ICPG 101.2.'

CAPCO duties per ICD 906 E.4: serve as central point of contact for all CAP requirements; 'Maintain the CAP Registry, a list of all control systems, including all compartments and sub-compartments'; 'Deconflict all IC CAPs or all other programs'; issue IC Standards; coordinate CAP-related engagements including congressional briefings, ISOO requests, and the NSC; and ensure at least one records official is cleared to all CAPs.
ICD 906 section D.9: 'The Director of the ODNI Controlled Access Program Central Office (CAPCO) is the accountable official responsible for the implementation of this policy'.

ICD 906 section D.9.b requires ODNI CAPCO to 'Manage a CAP Registry that maintains a list of all control systems, including all compartments and sub-compartments' and to 'manage all compartment and sub compartment names, codenames, and any other pertinent information.'

ICD 906 section D.9.c makes CAPCO 'responsible for the coordination of CAP-related engagements, to include, but not limited to, congressional briefings, requests from the Information Security Oversight Office, and the National Security Council.'

claims.text: An ISOO request about an IC controlled access program is routed, by directive, through the office that administers the registry of those programs - so ISOO's independent oversight of IC CAPs is mediated by the entity it would be overseeing. Reasoning: ICD 906 D.9.c places ISOO requests inside CAPCO's coordination function.

desc: CAPCO is the intelligence community's counterpart to DoD SAPCO and does two distinct jobs. Under ICD 906 the Director of the ODNI Controlled Access Program Central Office is 'the accountable official responsible for the implementation of this policy', serves as central point of contact for all CAP requirements, and must 'Manage a CAP Registry that maintains a list of all control systems, including all compartments and sub-compartments', deconflict all IC CAPs against all other programs, and 'manage all compartment and sub compartment names, codenames, and any other pertinent information'. It is also 'responsible for the coordination of CAP-related engagements, to include, but not limited to, congressional briefings, requests from the Information Security Oversight Office, and the National Security Council' - the same choke-point design as DoD SAPCO, with ISOO's access routed through the office whose programs ISOO would be examining. Separately, CAPCO publishes the Intelligence Community Authorized Classification and Control Markings Register and Manual, the document that defines the entire marking syntax used across the U.S. classification system, including the Special Access Program marking category. For this board the CAP Registry is the single most valuable unreleased document in the intelligence community: a complete list of every control system, compartment and sub-compartment, maintained by name, in one office, by directive.
